parallel.requirements: The run had the full prompt requirements: pure Rust 2021, std-only implementation, same CLI/default behavior, byte-identical output, root /output/test6.rs, library module files, and no C++ library source reading.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Despite swarm mode being injected, the main agent judged the task small and kept ownership of implementation, integration, verification, and delivery; no child owner was created.
parallel.implementation: The main agent wrote Cargo.toml, sortedcontainers.rs using BTreeSet for SortedSet operations, and test6.rs implementing the loop, bool formatting, and later exact atoi-style parsing.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The same main agent wrote the package root entry and module files, built a /output/test6 executable with rustc, and Cargo artifact validation later confirmed the expected files were present.
parallel.verification: The run compiled with rustc and Cargo, diffed reference output for n=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,10,100 and no args, then also diffed negative n; official evaluation passed 40 of 40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible at closure; the only coordination-relevant fact is that the parallel-mode run never actually used child or multi-agent execution.

serial.requirements: The serial run received the same prompt requirements for pure Rust 2021, std-only code, identical CLI and output behavior, root test6.rs placement, module organization, and black-box implementation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial main agent directly owned the entire solution, writing the project files, refining the parser, building, testing, and delivering the final response without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation wrote Cargo.toml, sortedcontainers.rs backed by BTreeSet, and test6.rs with Buffered stdout, then replaced the naive parse with an atoi helper.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial main agent kept the root entry file and module together through a Cargo bin target and produced the expected /output/test6 executable plus release build artifacts.
serial.verification: The serial run built with rustc, compared outputs byte-for-byte using od for no args and several numeric and malformed arguments, then built with Cargo; official evaluation passed 40 of 40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is visible at closure; the final response reports complete verification and the official evaluator confirms all testcases passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had the full test6 prompt, including Rust 2021, std-only, CLI equivalence, byte-identical formatting, root test6.rs, and black-box constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and therefore the same implementation, structure, formatting, and verification obligations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference appears; both runs ultimately handled the same requirements and passed all official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel entered swarm mode but the main agent stated a swarm would add cost and directly took implementation and verification ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no swarm context and directly took single-agent ownership of the same implementation, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only decomposition difference is the parallel run's explicit decision not to delegate; both runs were effectively single-owner attempts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created a simple local module contract between test6.rs and sortedcontainers.rs and had no child brief, child handoff, or cross-agent interface boundary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created the same local module relationship, with test6.rs importing sortedcontainers.rs and no inter-agent context transfer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No context-transfer or interface-contract difference exists; both interfaces were local files produced by one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote Cargo.toml, a BTreeSet-backed SortedSet module, and test6.rs, then edited test6.rs to replace simple parsing with an atoi helper.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same file set and made the same refinement from parse::<i32>() to an atoi helper before building.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementations are materially equivalent; minor code-style differences such as BufWriter use and a Default impl did not affect correctness.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results to join; the main trajectory proceeded from writes to edits, builds, checks, final response, and prompt completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were likewise no child results; the serial main trajectory ran the same single-result lifecycle through final response and prompt completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No lifecycle difference or join failure exists because neither trajectory produced delegated child results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a single main actor to write the entry file, module, and Cargo manifest, then artifact validation found the expected root test6.rs and build outputs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also used a single main actor for all writes and artifact validation found the expected root test6.rs and build outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision, overwrite, or contamination difference is visible; both final workspaces validated.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built with rustc and Cargo, diffed output against the reference binary for several values and negative input, and the official evaluator passed 40 of 40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built with rustc and Cargo, compared output byte-for-byte for no args, numeric, negative, and malformed inputs, and the official evaluator passed 40 of 40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used strong reference-binary checks and both official evaluations passed; serial tested malformed args with od while parallel used diff plus a separate negative test.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed normally without timeout in 108.421 agent seconds and closed with a final message after direct implementation and checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally without timeout in 87.152 agent seconds and closed with a final message after the same type of checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel took modestly longer, likely due to swarm-mode setup and extra direct checks, but neither run was budget constrained or left work unfinished.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial passed all 40 evaluated testcases. The runs differ operationally only because the parallel-mode session entered swarm mode and then deliberately did the work directly, while the serial session was direct from the start. Both produced a std-only BTreeSet SortedSet implementation, root test6.rs, exact atoi-style parsing, byte-for-byte reference checks, and valid artifacts.
parallel_contributors: Parallel-mode swarm was available but not used; the main agent completed the implementation and verification directly.
serial_contributors: Serial completed the same implementation and verification path without any delegation or subagent state.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel added a Default impl and release optimization setting while serial used BufWriter; neither difference affected the official outcome.
